title: First Connections
objective: Drive a circle’s radius with a slider.
learn: Inputs, outputs and wires: data flows left to right, out of one component and into another.

nodes.label: Radius
nodes.need: a value you can adjust by dragging
nodes.hint: Params › Input. You want a control that outputs a number you can drag.
nodes.correct: A Number Slider outputs one number within a range. Dragging it re-runs everything downstream — that is what makes a definition parametric.

wrong.panel: A Panel can show or hold typed numbers, but it is not a draggable control — you would lose quick parametric adjustment.
wrong.toggle: A Boolean Toggle only outputs True or False. A radius needs a range of numbers.
wrong.pointParam: A Point parameter stores a location, not an adjustable value.
wrong.*: This slot needs a value you can adjust by dragging.

nodes.need: a component that draws a circle from a plane and a radius
nodes.hint: Curve › Primitive. The result should be round — and it needs a radius.
nodes.correct: Circle builds a circle from a base plane P and a radius R. With nothing plugged in, P defaults to World XY and R to 1 — that is the small circle you see.

wrong.rectangle: Rectangle builds a four-sided curve from X and Y sizes — there is no radius.
wrong.polygon: Polygon approximates a circle with straight segments. Close, but the challenge asks for a true circle.
wrong.line: Line connects two points; it can’t be round.
wrong.*: This slot needs a component that draws a circle from a plane and a radius.

check.prompt: Which input of Circle should the slider’s wire go into?
check.hint: The slider carries a single number. Which input expects a number?
check.correct: R is the radius. With the slider wired in, dragging it resizes the circle live — try it in the preview.

wrong.P: P expects a plane — a location plus an orientation. A single number can’t say where the circle sits.
